critical_code_review_comments: server.py now 1071 lines — should be split into routers (chats, tickets, ai_agent, kb, canned) for maintainability.

run_llm creates a new LlmChat per call — session_id=new_id() means no conversational memory carried in the SDK itself; fine because history is stitched in prompt, but note that repeated non-cached calls cost latency (~5-15s each). Consider caching KB context per request to avoid rebuilding on every _ai_turn.

ai_email_reply / ai_chat_reply catch nothing — if run_llm raises, the /chats/customer-message and /tickets/ai-process endpoints will 500 with raw error text. Wrap in try/except and return a graceful fallback (e.g., low-confidence handoff).
extract_json regex '\{.*\}' with DOTALL will grab the outermost braces but can fail if LLM emits multiple JSON blocks or a stray '}' inside a string. Consider using json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode.
reply_ticket learning-capture uses substring check `'AI' not in body.agent_name` — a human agent named e.g. 'Nikhil AI Khan' would be excluded. Prefer an explicit `is_ai` flag on the request.

Training-insights ai_chats query is `$or: [{handled_by: 'ai'}, {handoff_reason: {$ne: null}}]` — the second branch also matches chats that only had a manual handoff (never AI-handled), inflating the denominator of the resolution rate.
HUMAN_REQUEST_KEYWORDS list contains overlapping entries (e.g., 'human', 'want an agent'); works but noisy. Consider a compiled regex.
seed_data_creation: Backend auto-seeds on startup; new KB(8) + canned(6) + ai_examples(4) seeded alongside existing agents/tickets/chats. Tests create TEST_-prefixed rows and clean up KB/canned via DELETE.
